text: 我真是服了，为什么都在说逼良为娼和强迫卖淫。
en: I'm truly exasperated — why does everyone keep going on about forcing decent women into prostitution and forced prostitution.

text: 这两个不是“卖淫合法化”的必然结果，用这两个反驳，只会让你的argument weak。
en: These two are not the inevitable consequence of 'the legalisation of prostitution'; using them to argue against it only makes your argument weak.

text: 作为某些人眼中的极端自由派，我是理念上支持“性交易去罪化”的。
en: As an extreme libertarian in the eyes of some, I support the 'decriminalisation of sex work' in principle.

text: 但是我来说几个作为自由派也必须承认的弊端吧。
en: But let me point out a few downsides that even we libertarians must admit.

text: 免得大家的辩论都在往奇怪的方向跑。
en: So that the debate doesn't all veer off in strange directions.

text: 性交易去罪化不能放在真空球形里，社会环境是否适合，社会大众能否接受也是非常重要的因素。
en: The decriminalisation of sex work cannot be considered in a vacuum; whether the social environment is suitable and whether the public can accept it are also very important factors.

text: 即使在性交易已经合法的西欧发达国家，比如德国，也没有完全避免人口买卖，和强迫卖淫的行为。
en: Even in developed Western European countries where sex work is already legal, such as Germany, they have not completely avoided human trafficking and forced prostitution.

text: 自由主义者往往用“这不是性交易合法化的锅，而是应该提升警力和执法水平”。
en: Libertarians often argue, 'This isn't the fault of legalising sex work; rather, we should step up policing and law enforcement.'

text: 这个也是不完全合理的，要警惕是否把自由的红利给了某个已经非常privilege的群体，而把自由的代价转嫁给了某个已经弱势的群体。
en: This too is not entirely reasonable; we must guard against whether the dividends of freedom are handed to a group that is already very privileged, while the cost of freedom is shifted onto a group that is already vulnerable.

text: 针对关于“吸毒去罪化”的argument也可以参照以上。
en: The argument concerning the 'decriminalisation of drug use' can also be considered along the same lines.

text: 现在结婚女方拿38万彩礼，一个月后离婚，彩礼不退，算不算卖？
en: Nowadays a woman takes a 380,000-yuan bride price, divorces a month later, and the bride price is not returned — does that count as selling?

text: 我认为公平是最重要的，如果认为花钱买x服务是违法的话，那么无论男女：
en: I believe fairness is what matters most; if you think paying for sex services is illegal, then regardless of gender:

text: 单次购买肯定违法
en: A one-off purchase is definitely illegal

text: 长期持续购买也要违法
en: Sustained, ongoing purchasing must also be illegal

text: 以购买结果为手段的诈骗更是违法
en: Fraud that uses the purchase as a means is all the more illegal

text: 这样才行
en: Only then does it make sense

text: 很简单，在一个二次元瑟瑟都违法的国家，谁给你的勇气讨论三次元线下瑟瑟的合法性？
en: It's simple: in a country where even 2D sex is illegal, who gave you the nerve to discuss the legality of real-world offline sex?

text: 不管二次元瑟瑟有什么危害，三次元线下瑟瑟都是它的十倍以上好嘛。
en: No matter what harm 2D sex does, real-world offline sex is more than ten times worse, you know.

text: 至于二次元瑟瑟到底有什么危害…
en: As for what harm 2D sex actually does…

text: 我是不懂阿訇们的脑回路，但你也不能无视他们手中的权力就是了。
en: I don't understand the thought process of the imams, but you cannot ignore the power they hold, that's all.

text: 现在的问题，不是你应该如何去反驳支持卖淫合法。
en: The problem now is not how you should go about refuting support for the legalisation of prostitution.

text: 而是先想明白，为什么卖淫是非法的。
en: Rather, it is first understanding why prostitution is illegal.

text: 但是很抱歉，我想了半天，在现如今社会通奸、包养、约炮、一夜情都是合法的情况下，我实在想不出任何理由要反对卖淫合法。
en: But I'm sorry — I've thought long and hard, and in today's society, where adultery, being kept as a mistress, casual hook-ups and one-night stands are all legal, I simply cannot think of any reason to oppose the legalisation of prostitution.

text: 你说卖淫是物化女性，践踏女性尊严所以违法。
en: You say prostitution objectifies women and tramples on their dignity, and that is why it is illegal.

text: 可问题是，服务行业多了去了。
en: But the thing is, there are far more service industries than that.

text: 按摩足浴技师（正规）也有很多女的，她们难道不也是用自己的服务取悦你吗？
en: There are many women among massage and foot-bath therapists (the legitimate ones too); don't they also please you with their services?

text: 饭店里大部分服务员也是女的，她们很多有时候还要忍受顾客的无理要求，甚至面对不讲理的顾客的谩骂都要受着，这难道不是对自己尊严的践踏吗？
en: Most waiters in restaurants are also women; many of them have to put up with unreasonable demands from customers, and even endure abuse from unreasonable customers — isn't that also a trampling on their own dignity?

text: 你在享受技师给你洗脚的服务的时候，在餐厅里对服务员呼来喝去的时候，对电话那头的客服人员发火的时候，你不也是把她们当成满足你某个要求的工具么？
en: When you enjoy the foot-washing service a therapist gives you, when you boss waiters around in a restaurant, when you lose your temper with the customer-service person on the phone — aren't you also treating them as tools to satisfy some demand of yours?

text: 你说卖淫会传播性病所以违法。
en: You say prostitution spreads sexually transmitted diseases, and that is why it is illegal.

text: 可问题是，恰恰是因为现在的卖淫行业都是非法交易，很多东西不正规，所以才会让疾病蔓延。
en: But the thing is, it is precisely because the prostitution industry is currently all illegal transactions, with many things unregulated, that disease is allowed to spread.

text: 如果合法化了，上岗体检、正规服务、专门监管，卖淫女和顾客的身体健康都能得到保证。
en: If it were legalised, with pre-employment health checks, regulated services and dedicated oversight, the physical health of both sex workers and customers could be guaranteed.

text: 这样岂不是反而能减少性病的传播？
en: Wouldn't that actually reduce the spread of STDs?

text: 约炮和一夜情之类的，都会传播性病。
en: Things like casual hook-ups and one-night stands also spread STDs.

text: 为什么不违法呢。
en: Why aren't they illegal, then?

text: 所以这个理由也站不住脚。
en: So this reason doesn't hold up either.

text: 你说卖淫会滋生黑色产业链，加剧人口贩卖。
en: You say prostitution breeds underground criminal industries and worsens human trafficking.

text: 可问题是，恰恰因为卖淫不合法，所以确实有一部分女性是“被迫”下海的，没有人身自由，就算向嫖客求助，嫖客也因为本身就做了违法的事情而不敢帮助她。
en: But the thing is, it is precisely because prostitution is illegal that there really are some women who are 'forced' into the trade, with no personal freedom; even if they ask a client for help, the client, having himself done something illegal, dares not help her.

text: 不是有新闻么，某个女性被组织强迫接客卖淫，向嫖客求助，这个嫖客也仗义，出了门就报警了，结果卖淫女是被解救出来了，组织也被端掉了，但是救人的嫖客喜提行政处罚，脸都丢光了。
en: Haven't there been news reports — a woman forced by a syndicate to receive clients for prostitution asks a client for help; this client is chivalrous and calls the police as soon as he is out the door. In the end the sex worker is rescued and the syndicate is busted, but the client who saved her gets slapped with an administrative penalty and loses all face.

text: 如果合法了，那么卖淫女的合法权益应该是能受到合法保护才对，谁还敢强迫？
en: If it were legal, then sex workers' lawful rights ought to be protected by law — who would dare force them then?

text: 你说卖淫如果合法了，那你会支持你的母亲、妻子、女儿去卖淫吗？
en: You say, if prostitution were legal, would you support your mother, wife or daughter going into prostitution?

text: 这就更不值一驳了。
en: This is even less worth refuting.

text: 掏粪工也是合法的，你会支持你的母亲、妻子、女儿去做吗？
en: Being a cesspit cleaner is also legal — would you support your mother, wife or daughter doing that?

text: 合法≠我想做。
en: Legal ≠ I want to do it.

text: 不要滑坡谬论。
en: Don't commit the slippery-slope fallacy.

text: 你说卖淫会导致群众思想滑坡，女的都不愿意好好学习正经工作了，都当小姐去了。
en: You say prostitution causes a decline in public morals, and that women won't want to study properly or do decent work, and will all become prostitutes instead.

text: 可问题是，包养也是合法的，那怎么不见大多数女生去被土豪包养？
en: But the thing is, being kept as a mistress is also legal — so why don't we see most girls being kept by wealthy men?

text: 答案是竞争。
en: The answer is competition.

text: 你的母亲、妻子、女儿为什么没有老板看得上？
en: Why haven't your mother, wife or daughter been favoured by some boss?

text: 因为没那个实力啊。
en: Because they don't have what it takes.

text: 长得要漂亮，要足够年轻，身材要好，性格要好，要提供情绪价值，要懂得取悦金主。
en: They must be pretty, young enough, have a good figure, a pleasant personality, provide emotional value, and know how to please their sugar daddy.

text: 那卖淫也是一样的。
en: Well, prostitution is the same.

text: 如果合法了，市场充分竞争，到时候只有年轻漂亮、服务态度好的女性才能在这一行立足，其他女人想入行，面试就被淘汰了。
en: If it were legalised and the market were fully competitive, then only young, attractive women with a good service attitude could gain a foothold in the trade; other women who want to enter would be rejected at the interview stage.

text: 要么低价恶意竞争，跟外卖大战一样，虽然姿色不足但足够便宜，用来吸引消费能力较低的人群。
en: Or they compete maliciously with low prices, like the takeaway price wars — lacking in looks but cheap enough to attract people with lower spending power.

text: 但卖淫的目的是什么，是挣钱啊，挣不到钱，那还卖什么？
en: But what is the point of prostitution? It is to earn money. If you can't earn money, then what's the point of selling yourself?

text: 所以，在那个社会，小姐是你想做就能做的？
en: So, in that society, is being a prostitute something you can just do if you feel like it?

text: 除此以外，我实在想不出还有什么理由要禁止卖淫合法化了。
en: Apart from that, I genuinely cannot think of any other reason to ban the legalisation of prostitution.

text: 我不嫖娼，我开过旅馆。
en: I don't visit prostitutes; I used to run a hotel.

text: 见过无数的嫖客和妓女。
en: I've seen countless clients and prostitutes.

text: 因为见得多，有所了解，我支持合法化。
en: Because I've seen a lot and understand the situation, I support legalisation.

text: 要登记注册职业资格，固定的场所和范围，并且依法保护，同时定期卫生和健康检查，并且建档。
en: There should be registration and professional certification, fixed premises and scope, legal protection, along with regular hygiene and health checks, and the keeping of records.

text: 不得隔三差五去收保护费。
en: They must not come around every few days to collect protection money.

text: 这样既提高了就业门槛（不是谁都能临时卖一段时间，又假装纯情骗个傻子接盘），又保护了以此谋生的部分人。
en: This both raises the barrier to entry — not just anyone can sell themselves for a while and then pretend to be innocent to fool some simp into taking them on — and protects those who make a living from it.

text: 还保护了大多数不卖淫的普通女性（泾渭分明，标签明确），和找不到女人的障碍型男士的性权利。
en: It also protects the vast majority of ordinary women who don't prostitute themselves (clearly delineated, with explicit labels), and the sexual rights of disadvantaged men who cannot find a woman.
